stories.headline: 'Lousy con artist': BJP attacks Rahul Gandhi after his 'foreign help' jibe at PM Modi
stories.bodyText:
Kesavan raised questions about alleged links between Congress leaders and organisations associated with billionaire George Soros.
NEW DELHI: Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) on Tuesday hit back at Lok Sabha leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi after he accused Prime Minister Narendra Modi of becoming PM and remaining in office with the help of foreign forces. BJP spokesperson C R Kesavan questioned Rahul's foreign visits and alleged that the Congress leader had sought foreign interference in India's internal affairs.
Kesavan also raised questions about alleged links between Congress leaders and organisations associated with billionaire George Soros. He questioned Sonia Gandhi's alleged association with the Forum of Democratic Leaders in the Asia-Pacific and sought answers from Rahul over his alleged connections with individuals and organisations linked to Soros.
He claimed that the secrecy surrounding the visits raised concerns over national security and demanded an explanation from the Congress leader.
Priyanka Jaiswal has four years of experience in digital journalism, news agency reporting and video production. Currently with The Times of India, she covers public policy, politics and global affairs. She is particularly drawn to human-interest stories that put people at the heart of an issue, spark awareness , and contribute to meaningful conversations.

stories.headline: Queues and chaos at many Tasmac outlets amid ₹10 price hike, shop closure rumours
stories.bodyText:
Despite the rain on Monday, hundreds of tipplers stood in queue for hours at Tasmac outlets across Chennai and neighbouring districts, fearing that more liquor shops could down their shutters. Salesmen at many outlets said they struggled to control the restless crowd.
On Sunday, many Tasmac shops pulled shutters down without informing the management. The reason: Tasmac had said last week that it will increase the maximum retail price (MRP) of all liquor variants in the State by ₹10 with effect from November 1 by adding an environment cess to the existing price. And tipplers can get this ₹10 reimbursed by returning the empty liquor bottles.
“We were given very little time to adapt to these two changes. We were informed only two days ago. Some of the bottles did not have updated price stickers. It was very difficult for us to scan them at the new rates,” said a Tasmac salesman in Vadapalani. He added that there were technical glitches and the POS machines and scanners provided to them did not work properly.
‘No space to stock empty bottles’
A salesman in T. Nagar said that there was no space at the outlet to stock the empty bottles. “We hardly have space to stand and where will we stock the empty bottles. They should have analysed the space in each shop before announcing this,” he added.
By Monday evening the crowd started increasing as fake news of uncertainty over the functioning of liquor outlets spread all over social media.
With Deepavali just days away, tipplers were worried about whether they would be able to stock up for the weekend. Tasmac, the cash cow of the Tamil Nadu government witnesses highest sale during Deepavali, Pongal and New Year.
Tasmac also suspended its workers across Tamil Nadu who were responsible for the shop closure on Sunday and Monday.
As on July 2026, Tasmac has 4,048 retail vending shops and a workforce of 22,877 (6,473 supervisors, 14,379 salespersons, and 2,025 assistant salespersons). For the year 2025-2026, Tasmac earned a revenue of ₹50,845 crore.

stories.headline: Disney weighs thousands of job cuts, asks managers to target 20% cost savings
stories.deck: Walt Disney is embarking on a significant cost-saving initiative that may lead to thousands of job cuts. Managers have received directives to pinpoint strategies that can achieve a 20 percent decrease in yearly expenses. This restructuring is a response to ongoing challenges in sectors such as streaming and theme parks.
stories.bodyText:
Walt Disney is considering cutting thousands of jobs and has asked some managers to target 20 percent in annual cost savings, Bloomberg News reported, citing people familiar with the matter. The savings could come from job eliminations as well as from reductions in other expenses, according to Bloomberg’s sources, who asked not to be identified because the discussions are private. The reported restructuring effort comes as Disney navigates multiple challenges, including the growing use of artificial intelligence, weaker box-office performance, intensifying competition from streaming rivals and a slowdown in international attendance at the company's theme parks.
Disney layoffs: Managers asked to find 20% savings
According to the report, Disney has directed some managers to target annual cost reductions of 20%. The savings could come from a combination of job cuts and other expense reductions across the business. The report added that not all parts of the company will be affected equally. Some Disney operations are expected to shoulder a larger share of the cuts than others as the company reviews spending across its businesses.
Disney CEO Josh D'Amaro plans reinvestment
The move comes under the leadership of Josh D'Amaro, who is reportedly seeking to redirect part of the savings into strategic growth areas. These include film and television programming, technology initiatives, theme parks and Disney's cruise business. The company has pledged to deliver double-digit growth in adjusted earnings per share during the current fiscal year, making cost controls and operational efficiency a key focus.
Disney lays off hundreds of employees, this is third round of job cuts this year
In related news, Disney laid off hundreds of employees across several departments in September this year. The third round of job cuts this year mainly affected human resources and IT teams across Disney’s corporate operations and different business divisions. Announcing the job cuts, Disney CEO Josh D’Amaro and CFO Hugh Johnston shared a letter to the shareholders.
The layoffs come after Disney warned shareholders in August that it was looking at more ways to reduce costs, including possible cuts to its workforce. The company had already announced major job reductions in April and July, followed by early-retirement offers to some longtime executives in August.
What did Disney CEO Josh D’Amaro tell shareholders
Disney's latest layoffs come after D’Amaro and CFO Hugh Johnston signalled that more cost-cutting measures were being considered. In a letter to shareholders on Aug. 5, the executives wrote: “We remain highly focused on reducing costs across the enterprise to create incremental capacity to invest for growth and are evaluating a variety of levers, including reductions in labor and SG&A.” They added: “We are mid-stream in this work and will provide future updates on our progress.” SG&A refers to selling, general and administrative expenses.

briefs.headline: Parts of Delhi reel under ‘severe’ level air pollution
briefs.deck: The 24-hour average Air Quality Index (AQI) of Delhi was 330 (very poor) at 8 a.m. on November 3, 2026, as per Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) data
briefs.bodyText:
The overall air quality of Delhi continued to be in the “very poor” category on Tuesday (November 3, 2026) morning, while parts of the city reeled under “severe” levels of air pollution, according to official data.
Parts of the city such as Rohini, Punjabi Bagh, Alipur, Bawana, Jahangirpuri, Vivek Vihar, and Narela witnessed “severe” level air pollution.
Many other cities and towns in north India, including Noida, Kaithal, and Hapur also witnessed “very poor” air quality, on Tuesday (November 3, 2026) morning.
The 24-hour average Air Quality Index (AQI) of Delhi was 330 (very poor) at 8 a.m. on Tuesday (November 3, 2026), as per Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) data.
The overall air quality of Delhi is likely to be in the “very poor” category for two days, as per the Central government’s ‘Air Quality Early Warning System for Delhi’.
The 24-hour average Air Quality Index (AQI) of Delhi stood at 324 (very poor) at 4 p.m. on Monday, up from 261 (poor) a day earlier, as per the Central Pollution Control Board’s daily bulletin, which is treated as the day’s AQI.
A higher AQI means worsening of air quality.
“Severe” level air pollution affects healthy people and seriously impacts those with existing diseases, as per the CPCB.
Every winter, air pollution spikes in Delhi-NCR and many parts of the larger Indo-Gangetic Plains, mainly due to meteorological factors such as lower wind speeds and a drop in temperature. Also, pollution from stubble burning during October and November and bursting of firecrackers during the festive season add to existing pollution from vehicles and dust, worsening the air quality.

briefs.headline: All 4,048 Tasmac outlets in Tamil Nadu to get bottle return machines: Minister Vignesh
briefs.deck: Minister for Prohibition and Excise K. Vignesh says tendering process for procuring the machines is expected to be completed within 20 days and warns employees against disrupting business at outlets
briefs.bodyText:
All 4,048 Tasmac outlets in Tamil Nadu will soon have reverse vending machines (RVMs) to facilitate the return of empty liquor bottles.
Consumers will be able to return bottles at any outlet in the State, irrespective of where they were purchased. The tendering process for procuring the machines is expected to be completed within 20 days, Minister for Prohibition and Excise K. Vignesh said in Coimbatore on Monday (November 2, 2026).
He told reporters that the government had taken steps to procure the machines to streamline the collection of empty bottles and ensure transparency in the process.
Referring to the existing bottle return system, Mr. Vignesh alleged that the previous DMK regime had collected ₹10 per bottle as party fund and another ₹10 towards the bottle buy-back scheme.
According to him, the government had stopped the collection of ₹10 as party fund and was initially collecting only the amount meant for the bottle return scheme. Now, the ₹10 bottle buy-back charge had been included in the maximum retail price (MRP) of liquor, he said.
He alleged that the number of empty bottles recorded as reflected in the accounts was higher than the actual number returned, despite the collection of the buy-back charge. The government had questioned the discrepancy between the number of bottles accounted for and the money received, he said.
Warning to employees
Mr. Vignesh warned Tasmac employees against resorting to protests and said strict legal action would be taken against those who disrupted the functioning of outlets. Notices had been issued to 960 employees, while four employees, who had allegedly asked shops to remain closed, had been suspended. An inquiry was under way into the closure of other outlets, he said.
The government was considering setting up larger shops measuring 500 to 1,000 sq. ft. to facilitate separate billing and delivery, he said.
The Minister said the revised MRP would be printed on all liquor bottles and consumers should not pay anything beyond the price printed on the bottle.
On private bars, he said a list would be prepared shortly and licence holders would not be allowed to sublet their premises. The government was considering relocating some Tasmac outlets.
On the possibility of handing over Tasmac management to private players, he said there were risks involved in such a move and the government had not taken any decision on it.

briefs.headline: Amid public backlash, Karnataka Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar directs Karnataka Milk Federation to reduce curd prices
briefs.deck: Though the State government has been justifying the price rise, hotel owners and the public have criticised it; prices being reworked and will be released soon, says KMF official
briefs.bodyText:
Amid backlash from hoteliers and the public over the price hike in dairy products, Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar directed Karnataka Milk Federation (KMF) officials to rework the price of curd and reduce it. Meanwhile, some hotels in the city have increased prices of coffee, tea and milk by ₹2 to ₹3.
The Chief Minister said, “I have instructed KMF office-bearers, who came to meet me on Monday (November 2), to reduce the price of curd.”
From Sunday (November 1), the price of curd for one litre, which was ₹54 earlier, has increased to ₹68, a rise of ₹14. Similarly, the price of Shubham milk and special toned milk has increased from ₹52 to ₹64.
When asked about the price variations across different categories of milk, he explained, “The price is higher for milk with higher fat contents. Officials will provide a detailed explanation regarding this soon. No one raises an objection when the price of a water bottle goes up — perhaps because the GST goes to the Union government. The increase in milk prices will provide support to 11 lakh farming families.”
Though the State government has been justifying the price rise, hotel owners and the public have criticised it, stating that the prices of curd and some varieties of milk have increased by ₹14. They questioned the logic behind it.
However, sources in the KMF said that the prices of milk and curds have been increased considering the expenditure incurred in purchasing it from farmers, the presence of fat, and other factors.
P.C. Rao, honorary president, Bangalore Hotels Association, said, “We understand the increase in the price of milk by ₹8 for one litre is to support farmers. However, the price rise of curd by ₹14 for one litre is beyond our understanding. Going by what the Chief Minister announced, the price of one litre of curd should have been ₹62. But for what purpose do hotel owners and every common man have to pay the extra ₹6?”
He further questioned whether this ₹6 will be paid to farmers or KMF. “Hotels, including vegeterian and non-vegetarian, use curd in various dishes including rava idli, lunch meals, buttermilk, raita for pulav, biryani, dahivada, Mangaluru bajji and others. The drastic increase in the price of curd has added 15% more expenditure to all the hotels,” he said.
Mr. Rao said that all the hotel owners affiliated to the hotel association would meet Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar and KMF officials to request them not to increase the prices of by-products like ghee and paneer as they were recently hiked.
Prices of imported bacteria culture increased
“The bacteria culture used in curds are of high quality and imported from West Asian countries. In the past five months, prices of imported culture have increased. The electricity bills have increased as products like curds have to be refrigerated, and petrol and diesel prices have been increased. The KMF has to give some margin of the amount to sellers or vendors in Nandini milk booths.
The official also stated that the prices of curds, as per the instructions of the Chief Minister, are being reworked and would be released soon.

briefs.headline: KEA to go ahead with written examination for recruitment of PU college principals in Karnataka on November 20, 22
briefs.deck: The lecturers’ association had submitted a representation seeking postponement of the examination by one month citing lack of time for preparation
briefs.bodyText:
The Karnataka Examination Authority (KEA) has decided to go ahead with the written examination for direct recruitment to the post of principal of government PU colleges as scheduled on November 20 and 22. The lecturers’ association had submitted a representation seeking postponement of the examination by one month.
The KEA is conducting the examination for direct recruitment of government PU college lecturers to 216 vacant posts of Grade A government PU college principal. Lecturers who have served in a college for more than 10 years are qualified to appear for the examination.
A lecturer from a government PU college in Mangaluru, who has served more than 15 years and is slated to appear for the exam, said not much time has been given to aspirants for preparation. They have to write papers on Kannada, General Studies, and Karnataka Civil Services Rules (KCSR).
The KCSR paper is a lengthy one and a minimum of one month is required for preparation. With lecturers being involved in SIR and other non-academic work, they hardly had time for preparation, since issuance of notification of the examination by the KEA on September 3.
Ninge Gowda, President of Karnataka State PU College Lecturers’ Association, told The Hindu that the last date for filing application was October 30. Like other recruitment examinations, the KEA should have scheduled the examination after a period of 90 days from the last date. He said representations seeking postponement were made to Additional Chief Secretary, School Education and Literacy, Rashmi Mahesh, and KEA Director H. Prasanna.
An office-bearer of the association, however, said there are no minimum marks, and top scoring aspirants will be selected for the vacant posts. After a long time, the government is conducting selection process for direct recruitment to the post of principal. Of the total 870 vacant posts of principal, 216 posts were being filled through direct recruitment.
“The situation is the same for all lecturers. It is better for aspirants to appear for the examination as per the schedule than seek postponement,” the office-bearer said.
Mr. Prasanna said the KEA will go ahead with the written examination as scheduled with 2,839 candidates expected to appear for the exam.

briefs.headline: Fire breaks out at HPCL Visakh Refinery; no casualties reported
briefs.deck: Reassuring the public, Malkapuram Inspector of Police E. Narasimha Rao issued a voice message that the situation was under control
briefs.bodyText:
A major fire broke out at the Hindustan Petroleum Corporation Limited (HPCL) Visakh Refinery late on Monday evening. The fire reportedly originated in the Pitch Tower of the newly integrated Residue Upgradation Facility (RUF). The sudden explosion and intense flames caused brief panic among residents in neighbouring localities, according to the officials.
Reassuring the public, Malkapuram Inspector of Police E. Narasimha Rao issued a voice message that the situation was under control. He said that HPCL’s internal Fire and Safety Department responded immediately with their own fire tenders to suppress the blaze, eliminating the need for external fire engines. He confirmed that there were no fatalities or injuries reported.
From June 2026: Fire and furore: On fire accidents in India
The RUF unit processes heavy vacuum residue oil into high-value clean fuels like diesel and petrol. High operating temperatures and dense petroleum pitch generated thick black smoke during the fire outbreak. Automated safety protocols allowed on-duty personnel to be evacuated safely while firefighting teams isolated the unit, preventing the flames from spreading to the adjacent facilities. Although no casualties were reported, structural damage within the pitch unit is expected to be significant.
When contacted, HPCL officials confirmed the incident, and said that a technical committee would investigate the exact cause of the fire. They added that the primary processing units remain operational and fuel supply chains will not be affected.

stories.headline: Pink Line likely to be inaugurated on November 13
stories.deck: The claim was made by a member of Parliament, but sources in Bangalore Metro Rail Corporation Ltd (BMRCL) said they are yet to receive a communication from the Prime Minister’s Office
stories.bodyText:
Member of Parliament for Bangalore South, L.S. Tejasvi Surya, on Monday hinted that the Namma Metro’s elevated Pink Line will likely be inaugurated on November 13.
Taking to X, the lawmaker wrote “November 13” with the hashtag #PinkLine, hinting at the opening. However, sources in Bangalore Metro Rail Corporation Ltd (BMRCL) said they were yet to receive a communication from the Prime Minister’s Office.
Last week, Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar said that the line was likely to be inaugurated mid-November. The government of Karnataka had been waiting for the Union Government to give a date for their representative’s availability for inauguration.
The elevated Pink Line spans 7.5 km, covering six stations, including Kalena Agrahara, Hulimavu, IIM-B, JP Nagar 4th Phase, Jayadeva Hospital, and Tavarekere.
The 7.5-km stretch, which is ready for inauguration, is part of the 21.3-km Pink Line. Once opened, the operational Namma Metro network will be extended from the current 96.10 km to 103.60 km.
The remaining 13.8 km of the Pink Line is an underground corridor. The underground section will connect Dairy Circle to Tannery Road via M.G. Road and Shivajinagar. When the line becomes fully operational, it will connect the southern part of the city with the central part, facilitating travel for many office-goers.

stories.headline: Bengaluru goes beyond ghee and besan, pairs Mysore Pak with cheesecake, chocolate, cookies and date bites
stories.bodyText:
In the royal kitchens of the Mysore Palace during the reign of the Wadiyar dynasty, it was Kakasura Madappa who created Mysore pak by mixing roasted gram flour (besan), boiling sugar syrup, and clarified butter in copious amounts for the first time. Now, this delicious sweet meat has become a cultural icon.
When autumn air turns brisk and the festival of lights draws near, sweet shops across the state prepare vast sheet trays of this golden confection. But something else is also cooking on the side. Just like how Dubai got its ‘kunafa chocolate’ in 2021 — when a chocolatier decided to craft a bar with a filling of pistachio cream, tahini and crunchy kataifi, the shredded pastry used in kunafa — the venerable 3-ingredient sweet is undergoing a vibrant, inventive culinary transformation. The classic buttery fudge is showing up as craft chocolate, baked cheesecakes, cookies and date portions.
Pushing the traditions’ limits
For legacy establishments, retaining Mysore pak’s authenticity while catering to the modern urban consumer is an exciting creative frontier. Explaining his brand’s pivot toward re-imagining Mysore pak two years ago, Sunay Bhasin, CEO of MTR Foods, notes that shifting consumer dynamics prompted the expansion: “There are a lot of people wanting to try out different kinds of sweets which they were not earlier either aware of or just couldn’t access.
”
MTR has added a range of different Mysore pak varieties that Sunay prefers to call “inclusions” — milk Mysore pak, kesar badam Mysore pak, kaju Mysore pak, coffee Mysore pak, chilli Mysore pak, and a portion-controlled Mysore pak date bites.
At Sweet Karam Coffee, member concierge Rohit notes that while traditional bases remain sought-after, infused varieties spark regular customer inquiries: “We have mango Mysore pak, and paks based on cashew and filter coffee.”
At sweet houses across the city, managers point to time-honoured mainstays. At A2B, the core festive lineup includes ghee Mysore pak, and kaju, badam and special paks.
Managers say requests for horlicks-flavoured and sugar-free Mysore paks surface occasionally, but demand during the festive rush is usually for the ghee rich, OG pak. Rather than turning to artificial sweeteners, customers seeking lighter options are actively gravitating toward jaggery-based preparations, says Sai Ganesh, a marketer at India Sweet House.
Cheesecake & cookie infusions
Step inside Bengaluru’s flourishing café culture, and the fusion turns even more daring. At White Teak Roastery in Yelahanka, owner Vasant has introduced Mysore pak into the café’s pastry vitrine by pairing it with classic Western baked desserts. “Right now, we’ve begun with the Mysore pak cheesecake,” Vasant says. “We are currently testing a Mysore pak French toast and a Mysore pak infused ice cream.” The cheesecake marries creamy dairy tang with the nutty, roasted sweetness of gram flour and ghee.
The reinterpretation of the pak has also caught fire in Bengaluru’s cloud kitchens. At Hazel Pâtisserie, co-founder Amrita has tackled Mysore pak from a textural angle by capturing the roasted aromas of gram flour and ghee inside a crumbly, crisp tea-time biscuit.
Cocoa meets royal heritage
In Nagarabhavi, artisanal chocolate startup Modello Chocolates — a women-owned bean-to-bar venture founded by Annie — is paying homage to both Karnataka’s agriculture and its confectionery legacy. Modello sources its cocoa beans directly from plantations in Hassan and makes small batches of chocolate bars. For their festive range, Modello developed the Mysore pak bar, bringing local ingredients into smooth harmony: “We make our own Mysore pak basically, and then we incorporate it into our milk chocolates.”
Meanwhile, in Mysuru...
Mysuru is ahead of its peers in the pak pivot. Mahalakshmi Sweets proprietor Shivakumar claims to have been among the first to introduce flavoured Mysuru pak, way back in 2000. The initial offerings included kaju, badam and milk flavours, he says. Today, the confectionery sells more than 2,000kg of mysuru pak daily through its 49 outlets across Karnataka, including in Bengaluru, Mysuru, Tumakuru, Shivamogga and Kodagu.
Among its 14 varieties, World of Mysore Pak in Mysuru has incorporated one based on kunafa chocolate, says store manager Rajesh. The store attracts an average of 2,500 customers daily. It also has an assorted half-kilo Mysore pak box, featuring 10 varieties.
At Guru Sweet Mart, proprietor Shivananda notes that flavoured Mysore pak requires more preparation time than the traditional version. The store sells 10 varieties of Mysore pak.

stories.headline: From jackfruit picantes to curd rice cocktails, Bengaluru mixologists are pouring savoury, umami-rich drinks
stories.bodyText:
Back in the day, a night out in Bengaluru mostly meant settling down in a cosy pub nook with a chilled beer pitcher. But a walk down the streets of Indiranagar, Koramangala, or Kalyan Nagar today would reveal a fresh shift. Bar tables are making more space for glassware that shows off intricately cut ice, awash in bright and shiny liquids that break all cocktail rules. Mixologists in the city are pouring differently, inadvertently birthing a new cocktail movement, and are encouraging connoisseurs to step out of the predictable zone of their sweet, artificially coloured cocktails for something more complex – savoury and umami-rich.
At The Reservoire, which pioneered the dedicated cocktail space in Koramangala in 2016 and later in Indiranagar, founder Prathik Shetty sees this evolution up close. “I think the best thing about Bengaluru is that people are so used to experiments and they want to try something new; they’re well-travelled.” He says there’s a huge demand for cocktails now, but what makes it interesting is that people are saying not to mix a sweeter drink.
 “Savoury drinks are doing really well, with umami flavours.”
To answer that call, bar shelves are raiding kitchen pantries and spice cabinets like never before. The Reservoire has tipples infused with Byadagi chilli, mahua flower, or roasted guava, balanced alongside Japanese pantry staples like miso and wasabi. Bartenders are even playing with pantry salts and coastal gems. “See, Tajín is basically like a salt... worm salt, sea grapes... That’s because it gives a nice, crunchy, grape sort of taste,” Prathik explains. He notes another powerhouse ingredient making waves across counters: “Yuzu is another ingredient that is trending... So, we do something called the Yuzu Paloma.”
Tajín is a Mexican seasoning blend. Yuzu is a tart, floral East Asian citrus, like a cross between lemon, grapefruit, and mandarin, used mostly for its zest and juice in sauces, drinks, and desserts.
For Satheesh Shankar, who manages the bar at Muro, the palate shift towards earthy and savoury undertones is unmistakable. From a shrimp martini to one with smoked pork, Satheesh’s bar team treats mixology as liquid gastronomy. Highballs have taken centre stage, and here’s why. “A highball is any drink with an elevated dilution, like a plain whisky soda... A highball needs the proper temperature and proper carbonation,” he says.
The trend extends far beyond the traditional party epicentres into emerging dining pockets like HRBR Layout. When mixologist Balakrishnan co-founded NoBa in Kalyan Nagar, he bet on the neighbourhood’s “well-travelled crowd” who, he says, shouldn’t have to drive to Indiranagar or MG Road to experience something new and big.
NoBa’s drinks list features a dedicated savoury section, led by a knockout that mixes tequila, mezcal, leeks, celery, oregano, and black pepper. “We have four savoury cocktails on our menu, of which one, called ‘Between the Lines’, sells more than water at the bar,” Balakrishnan says. “It’s a drink that is sweet, sour, savoury and umami all together... garnished with a watermelon pickle wrapped in a nori sheet.”
For many city mixologists, leaning into savoury elements is simply an ode to regional memory. At SOKA, unconventional ingredients are treated as intuitive seasoning. “To be honest, it never felt unconventional to us. We grew up eating salt, sour, heat and tang together,” says Avinash Kapoli, founder of SOKA, Indiranagar. “Chef Sombir and I both think of pickles and brines as elements that can pull a dish together, so it felt natural to ask what they could do in a glass.”
Their creations range from the Pi Pi Martini – featuring Hapusa gin, dry vermouth, and jujube pickle brine – to GSB, an unexpected drink inspired by comforting curd rice. “Nobody expects curd rice in a cocktail, and that is exactly what made us think, why not?” Other creations reinterpret everyday Karnataka kitchen staples, like Bandra Born with its dill (sabasige) cordial, and Jack Hash, which pairs a Mangalorean jackfruit dessert with cheese.
Spirits consultant Jonas Ax, who was in town last week to promote Patrón Picante, shares the sentiment. “Every city in India is putting its own spin on the picante, so for Bengaluru, we created a Karnataka-style version. We puree local jackfruit with salt and agave, then add curry leaf and pink chilli. The modern picante hasn’t standardised in India yet; it’s only been four or five years, which is why we’re making a different one for each city. Give it a few years and we’ll probably have a standard spec,” he says.
The city’s high-end speakeasies are pushing these boundaries even further. At ZLB23, the savoury movement takes the form of theatrical complexity: a ramen-inspired serve built around miso, sake, and soy with wakame noodles, alongside ‘Southern Ember’, a mezcal and tequila cocktail accented with tamarind and curry salt to echo South Indian rasam.
However, not every bar is rushing to make savoury profiles the centrepiece of its philosophy. On Lavelle Road, Bar Spirit Forward leans into classic cocktail architecture rather than culinary mimicry. “Personally, I’m not a big fan of all savoury cocktails. I do like Daisy styles, sweet-sour balanced drinks or spirit-forward drinks,” shares co-founder Arijit Bose. “But it is true that savoury cocktails have made a huge impact.”
With highballs flowing, mezcal lending its smoky allure, and bartenders embracing fermentation and house-made pickles, Bengaluru has firmly shed its one-note brewing reputation. The humble pint finally has some fierce, savoury competition!

stories.headline: Nobody has the guts, says HDK, dares police to take action against him
stories.deck: Kumaraswamy accuses Shivakumar of conspiring to distribute ‘sleaze’ videos of Prajwal Revanna; he accuses the Bengaluru Police Commissioner of acting at the behest of the Chief Minister and questions the objectivity of the probe in the sting video case
stories.bodyText:
A day after the Bengaluru City Police alleged that the ‘sting’ video targeting former Chief Minister Siddaramaiah was exchanged at his residence in Delhi, Union Minister H.D. Kumaraswamy on Monday (November 2, 2026) dared the police to take action against him while refuting the claim.
Hours before Mr. Kumaraswamy’s press conference, in which he claimed that no action had been taken against the perpetrators of the sting video, the Central Crime Branch (CCB) of the Bengaluru Police searched the residence and office of Power TV managing director Rakesh Shetty. The searches were carried out by multiple teams of investigators after obtaining a search warrant from a court.
At his press conference, turning the tables on Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar, Mr. Kumaraswamy accused him of having met and conspired with the accused to distribute “sleaze” videos of former Hassan MP Prajwal Revanna.
Accusing Bengaluru Police Commissioner Seemanth Kumar Singh of acting on the instructions of the Chief Minister, he told media persons: “Many people visit my residence, and there is no restriction on visitors. I do not know whom the Police Commissioner is referring to.” He dared the police to summon him for investigation and said that “nobody has the guts” to touch him. He also urged the Bengaluru Police to reveal the location from where they arrested a man allegedly linked to him in the sting operation.
Complaint by mail
He said there was a suspicion that the investigation was not being conducted objectively. “The woman victim had complained to the Karnataka State Commission for Protection of Child Rights. The complaint was not acted upon then. People behind the sting went to Kerala with the mala fide intention of meeting the woman for the interview,” he added.
Incidentally, Congress leader Kripa Alva was the chairperson of the commission from 2015 to 2018 during Mr. Siddaramaiah’s first tenure. Ms. Alva, who has been interrogated by the police, has been expelled from the Congress.
“There is information that the woman who had made serious accusations against the former Chief Minister has changed her statement. If this is true, why is she not being presented before the court? If she has changed her statement, she is part of the conspiracy behind the sting operation. She too should be named as an accused,” he said.
“Instead of undertaking the investigation properly, the police are satisfied with giving a clean chit to Mr. Siddaramaiah. Why are the police still investigating if the sting operation is fake? Why has the prime accused in the sting operation, Rakesh Shetty, not been arrested yet,” he asked.

briefs.headline: KPSC scam: Karnataka high court reconstitutes SIT, senior IPS officer R Hitendra to head probe team
briefs.bodyText:
Bengaluru:
 The high court Monday reconstituted the special investigation team (SIT) probing cases related to the Karnataka Public Service Commission (KPSC) recruitment scam, appointing senior IPS officer R Hitendra, ADGP (law and order), as its head in place of Alok Kumar, DGP (prisons).
Senior IPS officer Soumendu Mukherjee, ADGP (administration), will replace Divya Gopinath. The other three members — Anup A Shetty, Kushal Chouksey and Kshama Mishra — will continue on the five-member team.
Justice M Nagaprasanna said the changes were made after considering the names suggested by the state govt, objections raised by the petitioners, and the need to ensure an investigation that was demonstrably independent. Alok Kumar and Divya Gopinath had been named in the SIT constituted under the court’s Sept 21 order.
The reconstitution, the judge observed, must mark the beginning of a fresh investigation that inspires confidence and remains free from institutional or external influence. The objective was not merely to change the officers handling the probe but to ensure that the investigation itself was conducted with renewed independence.
The court also directed that no officer associated with the earlier investigation by the Criminal Investigation Department (CID), irrespective of rank or designation, be inducted into the SIT’s assisting team. The SIT will be free to select its own supporting officers and personnel, provided they have had no association with the earlier CID probe. The separation, the court said, must be complete in letter and spirit.
Govt has been directed to extend full cooperation and provide SIT with all necessary infrastructure, personnel, logistical and technical support, and other resources required to complete the investigation expeditiously, in accordance with the court’s Oct 29 order.
Embargo on transfers
The court also directed that SIT members should not be transferred out of Bengaluru from their present assignments in a manner that would hamper their work while investigation was under way, unless the court granted prior permission. Continuity of investigating officers was as important as their independence, Justice Nagaprasanna observed.
Simultaneous probe
Taking note of the Enforcement Directorate’s ongoing investigation following the registration of an Enforcement Case Information Report, the court said both agencies must proceed simultaneously, independently and in cooperation, within their respective statutory jurisdictions. The SIT and ED investigations should complement each other in the pursuit of truth rather than become competing exercises over jurisdiction, the judge said. The ED has also been directed to continue placing progress reports on its investigation before the court from time to time, in keeping with the HC’s Sept 21 order.
The latest directions are to be read in conjunction with and as a continuation of the orders passed on Sept 21 and Oct 29. All other earlier directions will remain in force and must be complied with, the judge added.
On Sept 21, while allowing petitions filed by Vijayapura MLA Basanagouda Patil Yatnal and others, HC had ordered the constitution of an SIT to conduct a fresh probe and complete it within 100 days.
The state govt subsequently challenged the composition of the SIT before Supreme Court, which allowed it to suggest alternative names in place of Alok Kumar and Divya Gopinath within two weeks. The apex court left it to HC to consider the objections, hear both sides, and decide on the replacements.

briefs.headline: Bring your tech, we’ll give you land: Karnataka government appeals to Japanese firms
briefs.bodyText:
Bengaluru: Karnataka govt has called for more Japanese investment in the state across industries. S Selvakumar, principal secretary, commerce and industries department, said the state offers more than a destination for Japanese businesses.
Speaking at the India-Japan Business Summit 2026 organised by Bangalore Chamber of Industry and Commerce, he appealed: “To every Japanese company here, the message is simple: bring your technology and we’ll bring the talent, land and partnership.”
Drawing applause from the crowd, he mentioned that Karnataka has long been one of Japan’s most active economic bridges with India. “With regard to technology, Karnataka is India’s largest chip design hub, with over 100 fabulous design houses, and 800+ research and development centres, making it the ideal place for Japanese companies to develop and localise advanced tech,” he added.
Hirotsugu Ueda, vice-governor of Japan’s Tokushima Prefecture (an administrative division), revealed that eight companies from Tokushima across various sectors are currently in Bengaluru looking for strategic opportunities. The companies, he said, included two regional banks, those from construction machinery, logistics clearance, glass processing and packaging sectors. “It will serve as an opportunity to expand the economic ties with India,” he added.
Hiroshi Nawata, consul general of Japan in Bengaluru, said Karnataka was home to more than 200 Japanese companies and over 500 Japanese establishments, reflecting the depth of the economic relationship between the two sides. “Bengaluru’s strengths in information technology, artificial intelligence, research and innovation complement Japan’s expertise in engineering, manufacturing, robotics and industrial excellence,” Nawata said.

briefs.headline: ED attaches assets, freezes bank account in counterfeit medicines racket; searches five premises in Bengaluru
briefs.deck: During the raid, the accused were allegedly found storing medicines and pharmaceutical drugs without valid licences, permits or authorisations and replacing labels on the stored medicines.
briefs.bodyText:
The Directorate of Enforcement (ED) has conducted search and seizure operations at five premises linked to persons and entities allegedly involved in a counterfeit medicines racket in Karnataka. The agency has also frozen a bank account containing approximately ₹9 lakh belonging to one of the accused.
The searches were conducted under Section 17 of the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA), 2002, as part of an ongoing money-laundering investigation arising from an FIR registered at Tavarekere police station on August 18, 2026.
The case originated from a joint raid conducted by the Drug Controlling Authority and police personnel at a residential property in C.K. Tandya village on August 18. During the raid, the accused were allegedly found storing medicines and pharmaceutical drugs without valid licences, permits or authorisations and replacing labels on the stored medicines. A Special Investigation Team (SIT) led by Vamsi Krishna, Joint Commissioner (West), Bengaluru is probing the case.
The FIR was registered under Section 318(4) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), 2023, and Section 63 of the Copyright Act, 1957. Since these offences are scheduled offences under the PMLA, the ED registered an Enforcement Case Information Report (ECIR) and initiated a money-laundering investigation.
According to the ED investigation, a man identified as R. Prashanth allegedly arranged a farmhouse near Bidadi to manufacture, repackage and relabel medicines without the requisite drug licence or permit.
Cheap bulk pharmaceutical formulations allegedly sourced from manufacturing centres in various States were repackaged into new vials and fraudulently labelled as expensive Pfizer antibiotics, including Zavicefta and Emblaveo. Although the vials allegedly contained generic medicines, they carried labels bearing the Pfizer brand name.
The counterfeit medicines were allegedly distributed through M/s DM Pharmaceuticals and supplied to M/s Krupa Healthcare. The latter subsequently supplied the medicines to other pharmaceutical entities and hospitals, mixing them with genuine medicines to avoid detection, the ED said.
During the searches, the agency froze bank accounts belonging to Veeresh Kumar containing approximately ₹9 lakh. Digital devices, records and other incriminating documents belonging to various persons were also seized.
Further investigation is underway to identify the extent of the alleged money-laundering network and trace the proceeds of crime.

briefs.headline: Global players bid for design, planning of Bidadi AI township
briefs.deck: Ahead of the finalisation of tenders, the Karnataka government has completed the process of issuing final notifications for all nine villages required for the project.
briefs.bodyText:
Even as protests by farmers opposing the Bidadi Township Project have continued for over 560 days, the Greater Bengaluru Development Authority (GBDA) is in the process of finalising tenders for the design and planning of the proposed first AI-powered township in the country.
Ahead of the finalisation of tenders, the Karnataka government has completed the process of issuing final notifications for all nine villages required for the project. The final notifications for the remaining two villages —Bairamangala and Kanchugaranahalli — were issued last week.
A senior GBDA official told The Hindu that tenders had been invited months ago through a Global Expression of Interest (EoI). “We have received bids from global players as well and will soon complete the process. The selected consultants will work with the Project Management Unit (PMU) at all stages of planning,” the official said.
Thus, both land acquisition and the tendering process are now gathering pace. The Bidadi Township Project, discussions on which had slowed over the past two months after Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar constituted a committee to assess its merits and demerits, has now picked up pace.
Recent notification
The latest final notification covers the Bairamangala and Kanchugaranahalli revenue villages in Bidadi. According to the notification document, a total of 1,142.25 acres has been notified in Bairamangala, of which 1,070.42 acres are residual land. In Kanchugaranahalli, 753.11 acres have been notified, of which 731 acres are residual land.
With these notifications, the government has now notified the required 7,357.36 acres of residual land. The project requires a total of 9,640 acres, with the remaining land owned by the government.
Farmers unhappy
Farmers, however, are unhappy with the latest development and have accused the State government of “backstabbing” them.
Prakash H.G., one of the protesting farmers, questioned the government’s decision to proceed with the project despite its promise to assess merits and demerits.
“On July 14, they had only constituted the committee, which also recently invited objections from all of us. Even before the report is out, these notifications have been issued,” he told The Hindu, adding that the government did not know how to keep its promises.
However, GBDA sources told The Hindu that work had not been halted and that compensation was being disbursed to farmers who were giving up their land.
“While a few farmers have been protesting, many other farmers were putting pressure on us to issue the notifications because farmers who were parting with their land were already receiving money. The two remaining villages also have the highest land values,” an official said.
According to documents accessed by The Hindu, farmers in Bairamangala are set to receive nearly ₹2.4 crore per acre.
The official also said that the land acquisition documents had been sent to the government before the committee was constituted, following which the State government proceeded with the final notifications. “It would be unfair to make farmers in these two villages wait. However, we will definitely proceed in accordance with the committee’s recommendations,” the official said.
However, Yashavantha T., general secretary of the Karnataka Prantha Raitha Sangha (KPRS), who is leading the protests, pointed out that the GBDA had given the same reason when it issued final notifications for two villages on the very day Mr. Shivakumar announced the formation of the committee.
“The Chief Minister had said on record that he would not touch the project until the report was submitted. This is a contrasting move now,” he said.

briefs.headline: Bengaluru: TDR process to go completely digital to speed up infrastructure projects
briefs.deck: The digitisation move has been planned to make the process of obtaining TDR more transparent and reduce delays, and facilitate faster land acquisition for road widening and other infrastructure projects.
briefs.bodyText:
Greater Bengaluru Development Minister Krishna Byre Gowda on Monday (November 2) directed officials to completely digitise the Transferable Development Rights (TDR) system, bringing the entire process under a single online platform. The system will cover the total process from application and verification to issuing the certificate and subsequent transactions.
Mr. Gowda was addressing Greater Bengaluru Development Authority (GBDA) officials at Vikas Soudha. The digitisation move has been planned to make the process of obtaining TDR more transparent and reduce delays, and facilitate faster land acquisition for road widening and other infrastructure projects.
The Minister said that the road widening and construction of new roads were essential to finding long-term solutions to Bengaluru’s growing traffic congestion. For landowners, however, compensation was being given through TDRs, while procedural delays in the system had affected TDR’s effectiveness in facilitating land acquisition.
Mr. Gowda pointed out that the existing TDR mechanism continued to depend largely on physical files. Meanwhile, the absence of proper tracking mechanisms and transparency had led to public dissatisfaction and undermined confidence in the system.
The proposed digital platform will cover the entire lifecycle of TDR, including the recording of road and property details, verification at different stages, scrutiny, and issuance of certificates. The purchase and sale of TDR certificates and their final utilisation will be brought under the online system.
The Minister said the platform would enable property owners and applicants to track the progress of their applications. The move will end the need for repeated visits to government offices or depending on intermediaries, he said.

briefs.headline: Contractors seek release of ₹38,000 crore in dues; Karnataka Chief Minister says valid demands will be addressed
briefs.bodyText:
The Karnataka State Contractors’ Association has urged the government to clear nearly ₹38,000 crore in pending payments for development works. Responding, Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar said the government was working to bring the situation under control and would address the contractors’ valid demands.
In a representation submitted to the Chief Minister on Monday, the association said bills for works executed since 2021-22 remained unpaid across departments, affecting nearly 1.5 lakh contractors and their dependents.
“There is an outstanding payment of around ₹38,000 crore. They have asked us to settle that amount. Over the last six months, work has been carried out and pending dues have accumulated. Now, we are bringing things under control,” Mr. Shivakumar told presspersons.
The government was holding discussions with Bescom, KPTCL and Energy Department officials. “We have accepted their valid demands and will resolve the issues appropriately,” he said.
Only assurances
Association president R. Manjunath recalled the assurances given during a protest by contractors at Freedom Park on March 6, 2026, when Mr. Shivakumar was Deputy Chief Minister. He had promised to clear the dues in a single instalment, the association said. At a subsequent meeting on June 30, after becoming Chief Minister, Mr. Shivakumar had again assured the association that payments would be released within two months.
The association said the outstanding amount was spread across various development departments and alleged a lack of transparency in tendering and payment processes in several departments.
It urged the government to stop inviting tenders for works without budgetary allocation and to take up fresh development works only after clearing existing dues. It also sought release of payments based on seniority, an end to preferential releases through special Letters of Credit, and scrapping of the package system, which it said disadvantaged small and medium contractors.
Other demands
Other demands include extending the eligibility period for work experience and turnover requirements to 10 years, releasing the 8% VAT-GST differential for 2017-18 and 2018-19, and clearing pending bills of Jal Jeevan Mission contractors.
The association also sought release of 25% of payments withheld for KRIDL works under the Greater Bengaluru Authority and a review of alleged irregularities in the Forest Department’s award of works under Section 13(B).

stories.headline: Oil prices edge higher after reported US strike on Iran's Qeshm Island, reviving supply concerns
stories.deck: In the wake of a US military strike on Qeshm Island, oil prices have seen a modest increase. This development raises alarms about potential conflict escalation, even as diplomatic dialogues persist. Both the US and Iran appear willing to engage in negotiations again, despite the failure of earlier talks. This situation continues to strain global energy supplies, particularly through the strategic…
stories.bodyText:
Oil prices edged higher in early Asian trade on Tuesday after reports of a US strike on Iran's Qeshm Island raised fresh concerns about the conflict, even as diplomatic efforts to end the war continued.
Brent crude futures rose 48 cents, or 0.5%, to $105.25 a barrel by 0104 GMT, while US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude gained 47 cents, or 0.5%, to $96.93.
The gains came a day after Brent slumped 7.63%, shedding $8.66 to settle at $104.77 a barrel, as markets weighed the possibility of progress in efforts to end the conflict.
However, reports of fresh military action have put the focus back on the risk of further escalation. The Wall Street Journal reported, citing US officials, that American forces had struck Iran's Qeshm Island. Some officials described the strikes as defensive, intended to prevent Iran from targeting commercial vessels in the Strait of Hormuz.
The waterway remains central to concerns over global energy supplies. Before the conflict began in late February, it carried around a fifth of the world's crude oil and natural gas. 
The sharp reduction in shipping traffic since then has kept supply risks elevated.
At the same time, both sides have indicated that the door to negotiations remains open. Iran said contacts with Washington were continuing after talks with Qatari mediators ended without a breakthrough, although revised proposals were put forward.
US President Donald Trump, meanwhile, cast doubt on whether he would resume threatened military strikes and said an agreement with Tehran was still possible. Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian also said Supreme Leader Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei had granted the government certain powers to pursue peace talks.
The competing signals have left oil markets balancing the possibility of a diplomatic breakthrough against the threat of renewed military action. Brent had already climbed to a six-month high at the end of October amid concerns over an escalation in the Middle East.
High fuel prices are also adding to pressure on Trump to bring the conflict to an end, with the war emerging as a key factor behind rising gasoline costs in the US.
Separately, Washington is scheduled to host Russian and Ukrainian delegations in Abu Dhabi on November 10-11 for discussions on ending the war in Ukraine, post-war security arrangements and de-escalation.

stories.headline: Petronet LNG reports 52.3% growth in net profits, in talks for availing undelivered cargoes
stories.deck: Along with their results, Petronet LNG also declared a dividend of ₹7 per equity share
stories.bodyText:
State-owned Petronet LNG reported 53.2% growth in net profits in the September-end quarter, driven by improved operational efficiency, although cargoes from its most prominent supplier, Qatar, continued to be affected because of the reignited conflict in West Asia.
The company also declared a dividend of ₹7 per equity share.
The country’s largest LNG importer’s net profit stood at ₹1,235 crore in the reported quarter against ₹806 crore in the same period last year.
Revenue from operations although declined about 35% during the period to ₹7,200.35 crore.
The company processed 231 trillion British Thermal Units (TBTU) during the period, higher than 228 TBTU it processed in the same period last year.
Overall capacity utilisation in the reported quarter narrowed to 64% against 78% in the same period last year.
Capacity utilisation at their Dahej terminal stood at 73% against 92% in the comparable period last year.
‘In talks with Qatar for delivery of pending cargoes’
Speaking to the press, Akshay Kumar Singh, Chairman and Managing Director (CMD) informed that the company was also in talks with QatarEnergy to secure delivery of the cargoes that could not be delivered because of the force majeure.
“On the sidelines, we also discuss if they would be able to give more cargoes before the contractual date. If there is a requirement in the country, we will take that as well,” he said.
The supplier has declared forced majeure until December-end.
Mr. Singh told reporters that the contractual terms have provisions to recoup the lost cargoes for one year after the expiry of the current contract period, that is, May 2028.
He stated that Petronet LNG lost an average 9-10 cargoes each month in the last eight months, thus, about 75-80 cargoes whilst it has received 6 cargoes from the supplier.

stories.headline: Chandra’s reappointment has sullied Tata Sons’ image: Darius Khambata
stories.deck: ‘The sad events of September 17, 2026, a day that will live in infamy, have sullied Tata Sons’ reputation and imperilled the image of corporate India. No amount of spin doctoring can mask what happened,’ said the outgoing Tata Trusts board member
stories.bodyText:
Tata Sons board’s September 17 decision to grant N. Chandrasekaran a third term as chairman has sullied the company’s reputation, outgoing Tata Trusts board member Darius Khambata has said.
Also read | Tata Trusts dissents to reappointment of N. Chandrasekaran as Tata Sons chairperson
Mr. Khambata expressed this view in a letter to Tata Trusts chairman Noel Tata while declining another term in office.
“The sad events of September 17, 2026, a day that will live in infamy, have sullied Tata Sons’ reputation and imperilled the image of corporate India. No amount of spin doctoring can mask what happened,” Mr. Khambata wrote on Monday (November 2, 2026).
“Would the board of Tata Sons have acted as it did on September 17 had Ratan Tata still been alive? Of course not. But duties are owed to institutions, not individuals. And as Ratan Tata used to say, the institution is always bigger than the individual,” he said.
Tata himself has opposed Mr. Chandrasekaran’s reappointment and has termed the board’s decision void. Mr. Khambata, a senior lawyer, has been a trustee of the Sir Dorabji Tata Trust (SDTT) and the Sir Ratan Tata Trust (SRTT), the two key shareholders of Tata Sons, since 2023. Within the organisation, Mr. Khambata has been an ally of Noel Tata on issues such as retaining Tata Sons’ private status.
The issue has divided the trusts, with fellow board members Vijay Singh and Venu Srinivasan supporting a share sale.
The SRTT continues to be under a regulatory ban. Mr. Khambata’s term at SDTT was due to end in November, and he is believed to have opted against reappointment in anticipation of opposition from Srinivasan and Singh. An executive with the trusts said Tata continues to hold a majority within the trusts despite Mr. Khambata’s exit.
Tata Sons declined to comment on Mr. Khambata’s letter. In his letter, Mr. Khambata highlighted key resolutions, including those opposing the listing of Tata Sons shares.
“Since May 2025, I have consistently maintained that opposition to listing must go hand in hand with providing liquidity to the Shapoorji Pallonji group through the sale of some or all of their shares,” he wrote. He also criticised Mr. Singh and Mr. Srinivasan for working against the trusts. “It is now untenable to argue that a nominee director of a public charitable trust, particularly a serving trustee, may act against the trust’s interests merely because he owes a duty to the company. He sits on the board precisely to protect the trusts. There cannot be two classes of trustees, those who are nominee directors and those who are not. All trustees owe an equal fiduciary duty to the trust,” he said.
(The writer is with The Hindu businessline)
