briefs.headline: FM Nirmala Sitharaman weighs in on Tata row: 'Should be resolved amicably, internally'
briefs.bodyText:
MUMBAI: Finance minister 
Nirmala Sitharaman
 said on Monday the dispute between Tata Trusts and 
Tata Sons
 should be resolved amicably, describing the salt-to-software conglomerate as a critical component of the Indian economy.
In her first public comments on the dispute, she said govt would prefer an early resolution that allowed the group to return to normal functioning. "I know the brand value of Tata, the contribution that the Parsi community has made to make Tata a huge global brand. I also know the expanse of activity in which Tatas are invested in. So, this is a very critical component of the Indian economy, and therefore it has to be amicably settled among themselves," Sitharaman said during a fireside chat organised by Financial Express.
FM Nirmala Sitharaman was responding to a question on the govt’s reaction to Congress LOP Rahul Gandhi’s allegations that it was attempting to destabilise the 
Tata Group
.
Rahul has accused the Modi govt of attempting to “criminally destroy” the group and treating Indian businesses as political playthings amid the dispute between Tata Trusts, which own the holding company, and Tata Sons, which owns the operating businesses.
Sitharaman said the matter required commercial judgement and cordiality between the parties. “I think these are very delicate matters and matters where a lot of commercial and business acumen will have to work. Business cordiality will have to work,” she said. Asked whether govt would intervene, she described the issue as sensitive and said she would not like to comment on it.
FM also rejected allegations of govt favouritism towards select corporate groups, pointing out that industrial houses targeted in parliamentary criticism were also welcomed and courted for investment by opposition governed states such as Karnataka and Telangana. On 23% growth in GST collections during Oct, she rejected suggestions that high revenues merely reflected a rise in imports (which had risen 42%). She said most imports comprised essential raw materials and intermediate goods required by domestic manufacturers to meet export demand.
The minister also rejected allegations that govt was creating instability or undermining democratic processes. She said opposition parties could not have legitimately won elections and formed govts in Karnataka, Telangana and Himachal Pradesh if elections were compromised or regime changes were possible only through street agitation.
She criticised the opposition for holding mock parliaments outside legislatures and walking out of legislative debates instead of using their constitutional mandate. With around 100 elected MPs, she said, the opposition should engage in debates on the floor of the House rather than walk out when govt’s responses challenged its claims.

briefs.headline: Darius Khambata to leave Tata Trusts, says ‘independence comes at a cost’
briefs.bodyText:
MUMBAI: Darius Khambata, one of Tata Trusts chairman Noel Tata's closest allies, will leave the Sir Dorabji Tata Trust (SDTT) and Sir Ratan Tata Trust (SRTT) when his term ends on Nov 8. In a four-page letter dated Nov 2 to Noel and Trusts CEO Siddharth Sharma, Khambata said he would not seek another term, even though both wanted him to stay. He wrote he was "saddened by the current divide" between Noel and N Chandrasekaran, chairman of 
Tata Sons
, in which the two trusts are majority shareholders.
Reappointment needs the consent of fellow trustees, and he said it was "not in my character to seek" it. "That independence comes at a cost," he wrote. He said his stand had at times differed from others, including Noel's.
His exit narrows the boards at a tense moment. SDTT will have five trustees: Noel, Venu Srinivasan, Vijay Singh, Neville Tata, Bhaskar Bhat. SRTT will have four: Noel, Srinivasan, Jimmy Tata, Jehangir H C Jehangir.
At SRTT, Khambata's term lapses automatically. The Maharashtra Charity Commissioner has barred the trust from changing its board while it investigates alleged breaches of public trust law. 
SRTT can neither appoint trustees nor renew tenures. At SDTT, reappointment needs unanimous approval, which would prove contentious.
In exit letter, Khambata defends key votes on Tata Sons listing and boardroom disputes, saying recent events vindicated his stand
The Nov 2 letter is the clearest account of Khambata's thinking. He said he was the first trustee to warn against the Tata Sons listing, calling it "existential" for the Trusts at a May 2025 meeting. He said he drafted the July 28, 2025 resolution, passed unanimously, that reaffirmed opposition to a listing while backing a liquidity solution for minority Tata Sons shareholder, Shapoorji Pallonji Group. The resolution also reposed trust in Chandrasekaran to engage with the RBI on Tata Sons' application for deregistration. Khambata said he did not believe that engagement had been meaningful, much less successful. A second resolution on July 28, 2025, backing a third term for Chandrasekaran as chairman, had since been "overtaken by the astounding events of Aug and Sept 2026," he wrote.
He also criticised those who "would decouple Tata Sons from the Trusts", calling the group a "national treasure in which neither limb is meaningful without the other." Khambata wrote that the "sad events" of Sept 17, "a day that will live in infamy", had "sullied Tata Sons' reputation". At the Tata Sons board meeting that day, Chandrasekaran was reappointed chairman for another five years. Noel opposed the move.
Khambata defended his vote on Sept 11, 2025, when he joined Mehli Mistry, Pramit Jhaveri and Jehangir in opposing Singh's continuation as a Trusts nominee director on Tata Sons board. The move prompted allegations that the four trustees were attempting a "coup".
Khambata had called that "absurd" in a Nov 10, 2025 letter and blamed a media-driven narrative.
In his latest letter, he said the Sept 11, 2025 vote was meant to strengthen opposition to any listing and that later events vindicated it. In April 2026, he said, Singh and Srinivasan told the media they favoured listing, despite having supported Trusts resolutions against one. Neither had explained the shift to fellow trustees, he said. That vote preserved Trusts' effective veto at Tata Sons by keeping Noel as their key representative on the board. Under Tata Sons' articles, he said, the veto works by a majority of the Trusts' nominee directors. The Sept 17 event showed how critical that was, he wrote.
Khambata said the Supreme Court judgment in Tata Sons v Cyrus Mistry validated the Trusts' special rights in the articles and the special duties of Trusts nominee directors. He said it was now untenable to argue that a nominee director who is a sitting trustee can act against the Trust's interests merely because he also owes a duty to the company.
Fault lines within the Trusts have deepened over the past year. Noel, Srinivasan and Singh blocked Mehli's reappointment to SDTT and SRTT in Oct 2025. Jhaveri did not seek another term at SDTT and left in Feb.
Khambata said he seconded Noel's appointment as chairman in Oct 2024 and was glad Mehli proposed it despite pressure to defer.
Khambata emerged as one of Noel's most important supporters as friction between Trusts and the Tata Sons board grew. People familiar with the matter said his imprint has been visible in Trusts' press releases and correspondence with the Tata Sons board. A senior advocate, Khambata first joined the Trusts in 2014 and resigned in Oct 2016, a day after Cyrus Mistry was ousted as Tata Sons chairman. His second stint began in Nov 2023.

briefs.headline: Govt listening to voices of concern in equity mkts: FM Nirmala Sitharaman
briefs.bodyText:
MUMBAI: Finance minister 
Nirmala Sitharaman
 has said govt is mindful of concerns among retail investors and equity market participants and will consider calls for policy support to the stock market, even as it seeks to sustain economic growth above 7%.
Sitharaman said the tax structure remained unchanged from FY24, when equity markets had seen strong inflows, but circumstances had since changed, with foreign institutional investors (FIIs) turning net sellers and concerns among market participants becoming louder. She said sustaining growth of over 7% required capital and govt was listening to demands for support to equity markets.
While govt had focused on developing the bond market over the past few years, she said there were now calls for similar attention to equity markets. "I do not want to say more at this point but I recognise the voice," she said at an event organised by Financial Express on Monday.
Sitharaman also said she was seeing a revival in private sector investment, with companies responding to visible demand following the rollout of NextGen GST reforms in Sept 2025. While businesses remained selective about sectors and investment opportunities, she said they were increasingly willing to expand capacity because they could see demand in the market.
"Industry today has the confidence that I'm able to see demand in the market. I can invest and produce and therefore reach the level which I want to reach," she said. At another event, a fireside chat with Hitendra Dave, chief of HSBC India, FM said govt would continue to drive growth through public capital expenditure while maintaining fiscal discipline. She rejected suggestions that it should loosen spending constraints or disregard fiscal deficits and credit ratings to boost investment.
She said public capital expenditure had generated multiplier effects by creating productive assets and encouraging private investment. "Capital expenditure remains a core engine of our growth strategy. Sustained public capex creates productive assets and crowding-in effects for private investment," she said, adding that govt would continue to support economic momentum through high capital spending. FM said fiscal consolidation and growth-inducing expenditure had to be balanced. "We will remain fiscally careful while staying creative and proactive in fostering sustainable economic growth," she said.

briefs.headline: Manufacturing growth eases in October: PMI survey
briefs.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: Moderation in output and fresh orders eased activity in the manufacturing sector in Oct, even as export orders rose at their fastest pace in six months. HSBC India manufacturing purchasing managers' index (PMI) released Monday -a high frequency indicator used to gauge the activity levels in the sector - came at 54.7 in Oct from 55.1 in Sept.
The headline figure remained well above the neutral 50 mark - which separates contraction in the sector from expansion - and above its long-term average, with the output growth easing primarily because of slower expansion among intermediate goods manufacturers, the survey said.
On export front, companies reported gains from a broad range of destinations, including Bangladesh, Canada, Indonesia, Oman, Saudi Arabia, Sri Lanka, the UK, US and UAE.

briefs.headline: Government assures Scotch importers of FTA benefits
briefs.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: Amid problems faced by importers of Scotch in bulk form, commerce secretary Rajesh Agrawal on Monday assured industry representatives that India will stand by its commitment under the trade agreement with the UK and ensure that the duty concession is not affected.
At the heart of the controversy is the import of bulk Scotch, which accounts for 80% of the whisky shipments from the UK. Under the trade agreement, effective July 15, customs duty has been halved to 75% under the FTA, which is to be reduced to 40% in 10 years. Bulk imports are crucial for blending whisky in India and bottling.
The Directorate of Revenue Intelligence has, however, been questioning the product classification of bulk whisky with the duty concession available to 220830 tariff line provided they are imported in containers bigger than two litres.
India assures Scotch whisky industry that UK trade deal duty concessions will remain intact amid bulk import classification dispute
Companies have been importing bulk Scotch under three HSN or product codes, 22083092, 22083093 and 22083099. DRI is examining if imports under heading 2208 covering spirits and whisky should be used or it should be 2106, which relates to food preparations that are not included elsewhere.
Industry is arguing that classification under heading 2106 will render the duty concession meaningless. It has demanded that the tariff concession should be available to finished whisky as well as bulk Scotch, otherwise Indian companies will suffer.
Govt officials said that the commerce and revenue departments will discuss the issue and seek to address industry concerns in the coming weeks.
"The ministry of commerce and industry today assured the Indian Alcobev industry that the ambiguity surrounding the current HSN code classification for bulk Scotch imports will soon be resolved amicably... The aim is to resolve the situation fully in due time and to maintain business continuity for companies in the sector," the Confederation of Indian Alcoholic Beverage Companies said after a meeting with commerce secretary Rajesh Agrawal.

briefs.headline: OpenAI takes steps to widen ChatGPT's reach
briefs.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: 
OpenAI
's push to reach more Indians starts with how they ask a question. Users who go straight to ChatGPT's dictation button rather than type are shaping the company's focus on voice, Hindi and other Indian languages, its India MD Prabhjeet Singh said.
India is already ChatGPT's largest consumer user market globally, according to Singh. Reaching a wider audience means making the service easier to use for people, who prefer speaking to typing, communicate in Indian languages or own entry-level smartphones. "Most of India actually doesn't use English as a primary. So real big focus is on Hindi and vernacular," Singh told TOI. Work on those capabilities through the year was beginning to show results, he said.
Alongside expanding access, OpenAI is engaging with the govt on data protection, model safety and cybersecurity. Singh said the company was making its models available as part of discussions on protecting businesses and govt infrastructure.
"It is important that companies, govt infrastructure is protected against potential bad actors," he said. "So, I think we are making our models available at different levels of dialogue."
He described the discussions as constructive, but did not specify which models were being made available, the recipients or the arrangements involved. Constructive regulation could strengthen confidence among consumers and enterprises and support wider adoption, he said.
For individual users, the challenge extends beyond language. Singh said OpenAI was working to ensure that smartphones with limited memory could deliver the full model experience. ChatGPT Go was introduced with affordability in mind.
The company is also looking beyond programmers and office workers. Singh cited traders using ChatGPT to create customised festive messages for customers and single-person shops exploring help with marketing and inventory management - tasks for which larger businesses can employ dedicated teams. He did not provide figures showing how widely small businesses were using these tools or the savings they had achieved.

briefs.headline: Powered by Reliance Industries' surge, sensex rallies 1.2k points
briefs.bodyText:
MUMBAI: 
Reliance Industries
' strong results announced on Friday evening, lifted investor sentiment on Dalal Street on Monday with the 
sensex
 opening over 700 points higher. After witnessing a sustained buying trend through the session, the benchmark index closed 1,233 points or 1.3% up at 75,693 points with Reliance's stock alone adding about 750 points, more than half of sensex's gain for the day. On NSE, 
Nifty
 closed 388 points or 1.7% at 23,441 points.
Sensex closed above the 75K level after nearly two months. At the close of Monday's session, RIL ended nearly 12% up, adding about Rs 1.8 lakh crore to its shareholders' wealth in just one session. RIL's 11.6% gain was its biggest single-session jump in the stock since April 7, 2020, when at the start of the Covid pandemic it had announced selling a 9.9% stake in Jio Platforms to global social media giant Meta.
The day's Rs 1.8-lakh-crore gain in RIL's market cap was the biggest single-session gain for a company ever, data from ETintelligence showed. In July 2023, HDFC Bank's market cap had jumped by over Rs 3 lakh crore in a single session. But that was the day after it merged HDFC, its parent, with itself and the merged stock started trading on the bourses.
Benchmark hits 7-week high after index heavyweight jumps 12% on strong Q2 show
The news that markets regulator Sebi had written to govt about the abolition of the long-term capital gains tax for foreign investors added to the positive sentiment on Monday, market players said. 
According to Vinod Nair, head of research, Geojit Investments, the domestic markets opened the week on a firm footing, supported by better than estimated Q2 earnings by corporates and improving domestic cues.
"Domestic macro indicators provided an additional boost to sentiment with Oct passenger-vehicle sales growth reflecting healthy festive demand, while gross GST collections increased, reinforcing the resilience of domestic consumption and economic activity. Global cues were also supportive, with softer crude oil prices and renewed US-Iran diplomatic efforts helping ease concerns around energy costs and geopolitical risks."
There are also talks that with the AI rally facing severe headwinds, the Indian market may again turn attractive to foreign fund managers which could, after about two years, again take leading Indian indices northward. The day's rally was aided by a Rs 3,115-crore net buying by foreign funds, data from NSE showed. On the other hand, domestic funds were net sellers at Rs 392 crore. The day's session added about Rs 8 lakh crore to investors' wealth with the market capitalisation of all the companies listed on the BSE now at Rs 482.3 lakh crore. Of the 30 sensex stocks, 23 closed higher, data showed.
US stocks rise
Wall Street's main indices climbed on Monday as oil prices tumbled more than 7% on hopes of a US-Iran peace deal, with investors also bracing for Tuesday's midterm elections.

briefs.headline: 'Cannot spill out in public': Sitharaman urges Tata Sons, Tata Trusts to settle dispute soon
briefs.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: Finance minister Nirmala Sitharama on Monday called the differences between 
Tata Sons
 and its largest shareholder, Tata Trusts, a “very delicate matter” and said both sides should resolve the dispute amicably rather than discuss it publicly.
Sitharaman said resolving the matter would require business acumen and cordiality. She also expressed hope that the group's leadership would settle the differences soon.
“It cannot be spilling out like this in the public. And for the maturity of that leadership, we would like to have this seen settled sooner,” she said, while speaking at the Financial Express Leadership Awards 2026.
Asked whether the government should intervene and bring the two sides to the negotiating table, Sitharaman said the matter required careful handling and declined to comment on possible government intervention.
“I think these are very delicate matters, and matters where a lot of commercial and business acumen will have to work. Business cordiality will have to work. So I wouldn't readily say, however serious the issue may be,” she said.
Highlighting the 
Tata group
's contribution to the Indian economy, she said the group had built a major global brand and had investments across several sectors.
“I know the brand value of Tata, the contribution that the Parsi community has made to make Tata a huge global brand. 
I also know the expanse of activity in which Tatas are invested in,” she said.
“So this is a very critical component to the Indian economy, and therefore it has to be amicably settled among themselves. So they talk it out to make sure that it comes back quickly to some normalcy. It cannot be spilling out like this in public. And for the maturity of that leadership, we would like to have this scene settled sooner. That's the view...” Sitharaman added.
What is the Tata Sons-Tata Trusts dispute?
Tensions within the 158-year-old Tata group had been building for months before coming out into the open at a Tata Sons board meeting on September 17.
The differences involved the board, led by chairman N Chandrasekaran, and Tata Trusts, headed by Noel Tata, the group's largest shareholder.
The meeting took place within a week of the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) rejecting Tata Sons' request to deregister as a core investment company.
The board decided to proceed with a listing in line with the central bank's mandate and also reappointed Chandrasekaran as chairman.
Noel Tata was the only director to vote against the decisions. Tata Trusts' other nominee director, Venu Srinivasan, voted with the majority.

stories.headline: Yashasvi, Rathod hit centuries as IND A vs NZ A 2nd unofficial Test ends in draw
stories.deck: Yashasvi Jaiswal remained unbeaten on 155 off 162 balls, while Yash Rathod scored an unbeaten 100 off 122 deliveries. The two left-handers shared an unbeaten 247-run partnership for the third wicket to put India A in a strong position.
stories.bodyText:
Yashasvi Jaiswal
 and Yash Rathod scored centuries as India A played out a draw against New Zealand A in the second unofficial Test at the Hagley Oval in Christchurch. The visitors finished their second innings at 282/2 on Day 4, building a lead of 204 runs before both teams decided to shake hands.
Jaiswal remained unbeaten on 155 off 162 balls, while Rathod scored an unbeaten 100 off 122 deliveries. The two left-handers shared an unbeaten 247-run partnership for the third wicket to put India A in a strong position.
India A were waiting for Rathod to complete his century before the match was called off. He reached the landmark with a couple off Rhys Mariu, prompting celebrations before players from both teams shook hands.
The match also saw more than 90 minutes of play lost due to rain on the final day.
Jaiswal, Rathod lead India A's fightback
India A began Day 4 at 32/0 after safely negotiating the final 11 overs on the previous evening. However, the visitors suffered two quick blows after play resumed.
Jarrod McKay dismissed Sai Sudharsan for 11, while Brett Randell removed Devdutt Padikkal for a duck in the next over. India A were reduced to 35/2 and needed a strong partnership to recover.
Jaiswal took charge and attacked the New Zealand A bowlers. He found boundaries regularly and brought up his century off just 119 balls. Rathod provided excellent support at the other end and gradually increased his scoring rate. The pair did not allow the bowlers to settle and added 247 runs without being separated.
Jaiswal finished with 15 fours and five sixes, while Rathod struck nine boundaries in his unbeaten knock.
Rathod's century was particularly satisfying after he failed to make a big contribution in the first innings. He had also scored 44 not out and 66 in the previous match.
The third and final unoffical Test will be played on November 7 at the Bert Sutcliffe Oval in Lincoln.

stories.headline: India thrash South Korea 8-0 to finish Asian Champions Trophy league stage unbeaten
stories.deck: Home Team To Face South Korea Again In Semis
stories.bodyText:
JALANDHAR: Unbeaten India finished the league phase of the Asian Champions Trophy with an 8-0 win over South Korea here on Monday.
Dilpreet Singh (8th, 40th minutes) scored a brace, while Jugraj Singh (11), Harmanpreet Singh (15), Shilanand Lakra (33), Sukhjeet Singh (34), Sanjay Rana (36) and Angad Bir Singh (60) added a goal each. India topped the league with five wins and will again meet South Korea in the semifinals. Malaysia will take on Japan in the other last-four contest as the action shifts to Mohali.
India built early pressure, with Sukhjeet creating chances. The breakthrough came in the opening quarter when Jarmanpreet Singh sliced through the Korean defence and Dilpreet Singh beat goalkeeper Kim Jaehyeon with a reverse flick.
India doubled the lead with Jugraj converting a penalty corner. Skipper Harmanpreet added another in the 15th minute. India carried the momentum into the second quarter, keeping up their attacking intensity and possession control.
Despite Korea's attempts to fight back, India's defensive organisation and superior ball control kept them in command with a three-goal cushion at half-time.
India made it one-sided in the third quarter with four more goals. Shilanand opened the scoring for the quarter, finishing a penalty corner variation involving Harmanpreet and Jugraj from near the post.
The fifth goal came from strong team coordination, with Harmanpreet's long pass finding Aditya Lalage, who set up Sukhjeet for a simple deflection.
The home team showed no signs of slowing down as Shilanand set up Dilpreet, whose effort the goalkeeper stopped before Sanjay converted the rebound for 6-0. Sanjay then turned provider, controlling Harmanpreet's aerial pass and driving forward before Dilpreet's stick touch made it 7-0. Angad rounded off the tally just before the final whistle.
Other results: China: 1 (Chen Benhai 2) drew with Bangladesh: 1 (Ashraful Islam 38); Japan: 2 (Kentaro Fukuda 24, 54) bt Malaysia: 1 (Abu Kamal Azrai 10).

stories.headline: Australia’s Glenn Maxwell calls time on international career
stories.deck: Glenn Maxwell, who had not played a Test since 2017, called time on his one-day career last year but kept the door open for T20s
stories.bodyText:
Explosive batsman Glenn Maxwell announced his international retirement on Tuesday (November 3, 2026) after being overlooked for Australia’s upcoming Twenty20 series against England.
The mercurial 38-year-old, who had not played a Test since 2017, called time on his one-day career last year but kept the door open for T20s.
He has not been picked since the World Cup in Sri Lanka in February, with selectors bypassing him for a series against Bangladesh in June.
Maxwell was again overlooked for the squad named on Monday (November 2, 2026) to play England in November, with a host of younger players instead preferred.
“A little bit sad and a little bit inevitable too, but I’m announcing my retirement from international cricket,” Maxwell said on the Final Word podcast.
“We probably had numerous discussions before and after the T20 World Cup,” he added of talks with selectors. “And it was pretty open-ended.
“There wasn’t any pressure from (Australia team management), and we decided to sort of leave the door open.”
“There was a couple of series that were coming up (in which) they were going to look to the future, and we saw that in Bangladesh with guys getting their opportunity and performing really well.”
“There was a small hope or discussion that I might have been able to potentially get a send-off game at the Melbourne Cricket Ground [against England]”.
“But I can completely understand the direction they’re going with this squad.”
Maxwell played 130 T20 internationals, blasting 2,897 runs with a strike rate of 154.42, leaving as Australia’s third-highest run-scorer after David Warner and Aaron Finch.
While he only played seven Tests, he featured in 149 ODIs, crunching 3,990 runs.
Maxwell also called time on his first-class career with Victoria, but will continue with the Melbourne Renegades in the Big Bash League.
“I’m grateful for the time I was able to play for my country,” he said.
“If you had offered me that career when I first walked into the Victoria change rooms in 2009-ish, I would have bitten your hand off.”
Published - November 03, 2026 05:44 am IST

briefs.headline: 'Chapter is maybe closed': Ashwin fears Bhuvneshwar's India career could be over
briefs.deck: Ravichandran Ashwin has raised concerns about Bhuvneshwar Kumar's return to the Indian team after disappointing performances. Bhuvneshwar, who returned after four years, struggled during the T20I series against New Zealand. He recorded just one wicket and an economy rate of 11.50 in four matches. Ashwin believes Mohammad Shami might now have a stronger case for a comeback.
briefs.bodyText:
Ravichandran Ashwin
 feels 
Bhuvneshwar Kumar
 could find it difficult to return to the Indian team after his disappointing comeback in the T20I series against New Zealand. The former India spinner believes the door may have closed for the experienced pacer and has backed 
Mohammed Shami
 to get another opportunity.
Bhuvneshwar returned to India's T20I side after a gap of four years but failed to make a strong impression. The 36-year-old managed just one wicket in four matches and conceded 180 runs.
Speaking on his YouTube channel, Ashwin said Bhuvneshwar's performances in the series were nowhere close to the form he showed in IPL 2026.
"Bhuvneshwar Kumar hasn't bowled that well; he didn't prove his form," Ashwin said.
"There was a night and day difference between his IPL form and here (New Zealand series). I think that chapter is maybe closed. It's very difficult. How will he come back?" he added.
Bhuvneshwar fails to make an impact
Bhuvneshwar earned his India comeback after an impressive IPL 2026 season, where he picked up 28 wickets in 16 matches and was arguably the best bowler of the tournament.
However, he struggled to carry that form into the New Zealand series. In the opening T20I, he went wicketless and conceded 49 runs in four overs at an economy rate of 12.25.
He picked up his only wicket of the series in the second match, dismissing Daryl Mitchell for six. However, he gave away 50 runs in his four overs.
The experienced pacer failed to take a wicket in the third T20I as well, conceding 40 runs. He missed the fourth match before returning for the series finale, where he again went wicketless and conceded 41 runs.
Overall, he finished the series with one wicket and an economy rate of 11.50.
Ashwin questions Bhuvneshwar's preparation
Ashwin felt the difference in Bhuvneshwar's bowling intensity and speed was a major concern. He also questioned whether the pacer had prepared well enough before the series.
"Leave performance, leave giving extra runs. It's not that. What was disappointing, I felt the way he bowls in the IPL - the intensity, his run-up speed was lower, and his bowling speed was also lower. That tells me maybe he didn't come in prime training form for this series," Ashwin pointed out.
He also explained why selectors could find it difficult to give an experienced player another opportunity after such a performance.
"If that's the condition, the selectors will also think, 'Is this the way'? If you're a new kid or a young boy, you'll get ten chances. But you're an experienced guy coming back," he further said.
Ashwin backs Shami for India return
Ashwin believes Mohammed Shami could now have a stronger case for an India comeback than Bhuvneshwar.
Shami has not played for India in more than a year and a half but has shown good rhythm while representing Bengal in the ongoing Ranji Trophy.
"Right now I'm thinking that the way Shami is coming in Ranji and bowling, he is in much better rhythm (than Bhuvneshwar)," Ashwin stated.
India's next T20I assignment will be a three-match home series against Sri Lanka in December.

briefs.headline: Blueprint under construction: India look to solve bowling puzzle in New Zealand
briefs.deck: With Bumrah, Hardik And Prasidh Absent, The 5-ODI Series In New Zealand Offers India's Inexperienced Pace Group A Crucial Chance To Stake A Claim For The 2027 World Cup
briefs.bodyText:
India have a fair idea of what their ideal ODI bowling attack should look like. What remains uncertain is who, beyond the established names, will fill the remaining pieces of the puzzle.
Jasprit Bumrah remains India's undisputed spearhead, while 
Mohammed Siraj
 is the closest thing to a settled second seamer. Beyond that, however, the pecking order is far from finalised. 
Arshdeep Singh
's left-arm variety has made him a proven force in T20Is, but he is still relatively untested in the 50-over format. Gurnoor Brar is only beginning to find his feet, while India's search for a reliable pace-bowling all-rounder capable of easing the dependence on Hardik Pandya remains unresolved.
That is why the five-match ODI series against New Zealand, beginning in Auckland on Wednesday, carries significance far beyond a routine bilateral contest. With the 2027 ODI World Cup in South Africa now less than a year away, India are running out of opportunities to answer some critical questions about their bowling resources.
The absence of Bumrah and Pandya from the tour has already shifted greater responsibility onto a young attack. 
The blow was compounded by Prasidh Krishna's hamstring injury, ruling out a bowler widely viewed as a near-certain World Cup pick, especially given the fact that he is a tall, hit-the-deck bowler, the kind that does well on pitches in South Africa.
Siraj, with 51 ODIs behind him, becomes the senior figure in the pace unit. Around him are bowlers rich in promise but short on experience. Arshdeep has played just 18 ODIs, Gurnoor only nine, while Auqib Nabi and Anshul Kamboj are still trying to establish themselves at the international level.
Head coach 
Gautam Gambhir
 was unusually frank when he described the group as potentially India's "most inexperienced ODI bowling attack". His assessment also underscored the importance of the assignment. If India prosper in New Zealand, it will be because this attack has risen to the challenge in conditions not traditionally in India's comfort zone.
Beyond evaluating individuals, India must identify specialists for every phase of an ODI innings: new-ball operators, middle-overs enforcers, bowlers who can bowl dry and death-bowling finishers. Equally important is finding combinations that can succeed in conditions similar to those expected in South Africa.
And when one talks about weaknesses, the seam-bowling all-rounder question springs up. Nitish Kumar Reddy has emerged as a possible backup to Hardik and in the T20Is, one saw him bowl the difficult overs and bowl with increased pace and effectiveness, but with only eight ODIs and limited evidence of his effectiveness as a fifth bowling option, he remains a work in progress. He will also be featuring in only the first ODI as India are looking to play him in the Test matches.
The batting unit, though, gives greater comfort and offers greater certainty. Questions around Rohit Sharma and Virat Kohli's future have gradually given way to discussions on how best to maximise their experience. Shubman Gill, meanwhile, has an opportunity to strengthen his credentials as ODI captain, leading in the first three matches before Shreyas Iyer takes charge for the final two as Gill prepares for Tests.
For India, this tour is less about immediate results and more about gaining much-needed clarity. The World Cup blueprint is taking shape. The bowlers now have five matches to prove they belong in it.
"If we do well in the One-day series, the credit will go to this bowling attack. It will go to these boys. When you come overseas, your bowlers win the series, especially in One-day and Test cricket," Gambhir stressed.
India have three ODIs against Sri Lanka in Dec and another three against Zimbabwe in Jan. But those games are in Indian conditions which are vastly different from South Africa. If the team has to identify weaknesses and address them, it has to be here, in New Zealand.

briefs.headline: 'Hopefully he plays some domestic': Shubman Gill gives update on Hardik Pandya's comeback
briefs.deck: Hardik Pandya has not played for the Indian team since the 2026 T20 World Cup final. He has missed several international matches due to fitness concerns, including tours of Ireland and England. Captain Shubman Gill emphasized Pandya's importance for strengthening India's batting order. The team management is in regular contact with Pandya about his fitness and recovery plans.
briefs.bodyText:
When will 
Hardik Pandya
 return to the Indian team? How is the all-rounder's fitness? When will he be seen wearing India colours again?
These were some of the questions put to India captain Shubman Gill during his press conference ahead of the first ODI against New Zealand in Auckland on Wednesday.
Pandya's absence from international cricket has been a talking point, with fans waiting for an update on his return. The all-rounder last represented India in the 2026 T20 World Cup final in Ahmedabad. Since then, his only competitive appearances have come in the Indian Premier League for Mumbai Indians.
Pandya has missed several international assignments since the T20 World Cup, including India's home series against Afghanistan and tours of Ireland and England. He was also unavailable for the home ODI series against the West Indies and is missing the ongoing tour of New Zealand.
Gill said the team management has been in regular touch with Pandya and highlighted the importance of having a player of his ability in the side.
He also revealed that the all-rounder suffered a niggle before the India A match.
"We have had multiple conversations, he is a quality player - not many in the world have what he can do. 
Hopefully he plays some domestic and gets back. Unfortunate he got a niggle before India A match," Gill told reporters ahead of the first ODI.
Hardik's return to solve India's lower-order concerns
Gill also explained how Pandya's return would help India strengthen their lower order. The captain believes the all-rounder's presence would take care of the No. 7 and No. 8 batting positions.
"Whenever Hardik bhai comes back, no 7/8 will also be taken care of. Happy with batting group leading up to the ODI World Cup," he said.
India will begin their five-match ODI series against New Zealand at Eden Park in Auckland on November 4. The second match will be played in Wellington on November 7, followed by the third ODI in Hamilton on November 10.
The teams will then move to Mount Maunganui for the final two matches on November 13 and 15.

briefs.bodyText:
India captain Shubman Gill has outlined the team's plans for the middle order ahead of the five-match ODI series against New Zealand. Gill said India will adopt a flexible approach for the No. 5 and No. 6 positions, with 
Axar Patel
 and 
KL Rahul
 expected to take up these roles depending on the match situation.
India will begin the series against New Zealand on Wednesday at Eden Park in Auckland. According to Gill, the top four batting positions are settled, while the team is open to making changes in the middle order.
"We will have floating approach for no.5 and no.6. Our top four is set, all right-handers. So if lefty is needed, Axar bhai goes and depending on match situation even KL bhai can go. So bit flexible," Gill said ahead of the opening ODI match.
Gill plays down concerns over neck issue
Gill also dismissed concerns about his neck, which had troubled him in the past.
The India captain suffered a cervical disc bulge and neck spasm that affected his nerves in late 2025. The injury kept him out of international cricket for nearly a month.
He had suffered the injury on the second day of the Kolkata Test against South Africa and was taken to hospital for examination after the day's play. 
He remained under observation and was discharged the following day before travelling to Guwahati on November 19, 2025.
However, Gill said he was not experiencing any discomfort and had completed his batting and fielding duties without any problems.
"No issue… I batter for close to one and a half hours and did my fielding without any trouble too. No issue at all," he said.

briefs.headline: Rajat Paliwal's 21st first-class ton: A century without knowing he was nearing one
briefs.deck: Ravikant has operated the manual scoreboard at Palam's Air Force Complex Ground for 35 years, but one batter's name has been missing since cricket resumed after Covid. Services captain Rajat Paliwal prefers not to see his name while batting, a superstition he believes helps him concentrate. On Monday, he struck his 21st first-class century to rescue Services against Delhi.
briefs.bodyText:
NEW DELHI:
 Ravikant has kept Palam's Air Force Complex Ground ticking for the past 35 years. The chief ground staff member, he also doubles up as the scoreboard operator. But when cricket resumed after the COVID pandemic, he received an unusual request from the Services captain Rajat Paliwal: he did not want his name displayed on the scoreboard while batting.
Ravikant, a little hesitant at first, agreed.
"Sab ka apna apna hota hai. Kaptaan sahab ka farman aaya aur humne maan liya (Everyone has their own superstition. He made the request and I accepted it)," Ravikant said.
On Monday, the 34-year-old Paliwal smashed his 21st first-class century to rescue Services, who were reeling at 27 for three, and took them to 266 on the opening day of their 
Ranji Trophy
 Group C clash against Delhi. He remained unbeaten on 111 off 196 balls.
With no name appearing against Batsman 2 (Paliwal) on the scoreboard, the veteran batter had no way of knowing how close he was to his century. He eventually realised he had reached the milestone through the reaction of Delhi's fielders, who began closing in around him.
"I got to know that I was getting closer to a century when I saw more fielders around me. I realised I had scored a hundred only through the reaction of the Delhi players," he told reporters at the end of the opening day.
The manual scorecard at Palam's Air Force Complex Ground in New Delhi. (Photo: Pratyush Raj)
"I started this practice sometime after Covid. Sometimes, I used to feel a little nervous and lose my focus. The scoreboard draws attention, so I have taken it out of the picture entirely to concentrate only on the game," he added.
This was Paliwal's highest score of the season so far, and he described it as particularly special. When he walked out to bat, Services were staring at the possibility of being bowled out for less than 100. But Paliwal stood up for his team, as he has done for nearly a decade-and-a-half.
"This hundred is very special, especially because the team had lost four wickets for 44 runs and we needed this knock. This has come after a long time and at a critical juncture before a break, to set the tone for the next phase," he said.
Yes, I look at Paras as an example. He has crossed 10,000 runs in first-class cricket and has been remarkably consistent. Last year, he also won the Ranji Trophy title. His persistence and consistency are inspiring.
Rajat Paliwal on Paras Dogra
Paliwal, who turns 35 in December, knows that his chances of breaking into the Indian team are now limited. However, he continues to draw inspiration from Jammu and Kashmir captain 
Paras Dogra
, 41, with whom he remains in regular touch.
"Yes, I look at Paras as an example. He has crossed 10,000 runs in first-class cricket and has been remarkably consistent. Last year, he also won the Ranji Trophy title. His persistence and consistency are inspiring. Paras has been an inspiration in this regard. He became a Ranji Trophy champion in his forties. When you see him consistently performing at that age, you feel confident about yourself as well," he said.
"Yashpal [Singh] is another player who has influenced me a lot. He scored a lot of runs and played alongside me for four or five years when I started. We had some very good partnerships together," he added.
Nagpur: Services batter Rajat Paliwal plays a shot during the first day of the Ranji Trophy cricket match between Services and Vidarbha, in Nagpur. (PTI Photo)(
A bulwark of India's domestic cricket circuit, Paliwal believes that the love for first-class cricket in the country is far from fading. He cited his Delhi counterpart, 
Ayush Badoni
, who has scored back-to-back double centuries, as an example of the continued appetite for the longer format.
"It's true that cricket has become much faster. Throughout the year, there is a lot of focus on T20 cricket because of the exposure, media coverage and attention it receives. But you cannot categorise players like that. If you look at Badoni, he has scored two double centuries on the trot. Badoni is my opponent, but I would like to appreciate him because it is not easy to score back-to-back double hundreds.
"Every player has individual priorities, and everyone approaches the game differently. Everyone has their own preferences and ambitions. Some want to establish themselves in this format, while others prefer the shorter formats. But I believe many players still try to perform in the longest format as well," he continued.

briefs.headline: 'The Big Show' is over: Glenn Maxwell announces retirement from international cricket
briefs.deck: Maxwell, popularly known as 'The Big Show', represented Australia in 149 ODIs, 130 T20Is and seven Test matches. He was part of Australia's 2015 and 2023 ODI World Cup-winning teams and also played a key role in the team's T20 World Cup triumph in 2021.
briefs.bodyText:
Australian all-rounder 
Glenn Maxwell
 has announced his retirement from international cricket, bringing an end to a career in which he entertained fans with his aggressive batting and unusual shots. Maxwell made the announcement on Tuesday during an episode of The Final Word podcast. His decision also includes his retirement from domestic 50-over and four-day cricket for Victoria.
Maxwell, popularly known as 'The Big Show', represented Australia in 149 ODIs, 130 T20Is and seven Test matches. He was part of Australia's 2015 and 2023 ODI World Cup-winning teams and also played a key role in the team's T20 World Cup triumph in 2021.
"I'm going to be announcing my retirement from international cricket and domestic games for Victoria in the 50 over and the four-day stuff, red ball completely," the 38-year-old told The Final Word podcast in an episode released on Tuesday.
Wants to focus on fitness
Maxwell said he wants to give more attention to his fitness and prepare his body for the remaining tournaments in his career.
"It's probably a time where I probably need to spend a little bit more time investing in the body to make sure I can get through the remaining couple of tournaments I've got in my career."
He scored 3,990 runs in ODIs and 2,897 runs in T20 internationals. His last appearance for Australia came against Oman at the T20 World Cup in Sri Lanka in February.
Maxwell also made a special mark in T20 cricket. Along with India's Rohit Sharma, he remains one of only two players to score five international centuries in the format.
With his off-spin bowling, he also picked up 128 wickets for Australia in the two shorter formats.
Misses chance for MCG farewell
Maxwell had retired from ODI cricket last year but was hoping to play one final international match at the Melbourne Cricket Ground (MCG).
However, that possibility ended when Australia announced its squad for the upcoming series against England on Monday. The selectors have focused on younger players in their short-format plans.
Maxwell admitted that he had hoped to get a farewell match at his home ground but understood the team's decision.
"There was, I suppose, a small hope or discussion that I might have been able to potentially get a send-off game at the MCG, but I can completely understand the direction they're going with this squad," he said.

briefs.headline: Gymnast, seamstress, Olympian... the many lives of Casey Kaufhold
briefs.deck: I am naturally competitive, but the enjoyment aspect has always stayed with me. I think that has led me to a lot of success
briefs.bodyText:
Before big competitions, Casey Kaufhold plays a song. Her go-to is “Don’t stop me now” by Queen, a three-minute declaration of unstoppable joy. briefs.headline: IPL retention deadline extended to November 17
briefs.deck: The extension is understood to have been prompted by the India-New Zealand ODI series, with the fifth and final match scheduled to be played on November 15
briefs.bodyText:
The Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) has extended the deadline for the Indian Premier League (IPL) franchises to submit the player retention list by two days, giving them until November 17 to finalise their squads ahead of the mini auction in Goa on December 16.
In a communication shared with the franchises on Monday, the BCCI informed them of the revised deadline, replacing the original November 15 cut-off.
The extension is understood to have been prompted by the India-New Zealand ODI series, with the fifth and final match scheduled to be played at the Bay Oval in Mount Maunganui on November 15. Interestingly, the auction itself will coincide with India’s second ODI against Sri Lanka at the M. Chinnaswamy Stadium in Bengaluru.
The BCCI has also outlined the timeline leading up to the auction. Player registration opened on Monday and will close on November 23. Franchises will have until December 1 to submit the list of players they wish to bid for, before the final auction register, including the order of player sets, will be released on December 3.
The transfer market expected to see frenetic activity in the coming fortnight.
